title: Raila’s comparative postal-accident hypotheticals
summary: The panel tested the government’s proposed immunity rule by comparing injuries whose differences appeared unrelated to the statute’s purpose.
notes:
First compare two pedestrians: a postal driver throws a parcel that strikes one, while the driver’s simultaneous inattention causes the truck to strike the other. Next compare two post-office customers: one slips on liquid spilled from a mishandled parcel and another slips on water negligently left by a janitor. Ask whether the postal-matter exception supplies a reason to immunize one injury in each pair while allowing suit for the other.

The government acknowledged that its reading would distinguish the paired injuries. The panel regarded those distinctions as absurd in context and as a reason to reject that interpretation. These are the judges’ hypothetical examples, not findings about Raila’s accident, and no separate negligence judgment follows from them. A careful answer should tie the anomaly argument to the text, neighboring terms, and overall waiver rather than invoke fairness alone.
